diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\E[\bm Y| \XX] = \E[\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm b]$ is not necessarily in $\col(\bm X)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition is stated as necessary, but it is only sufficient in general. For example, take Ω=[-1,1], μ uniform, V_n=span{1,x}, f(x)=x^2, and sample points x_1=-1, x_2=1. Then f^*=2/3, so f-f^* does not vanish at the sample points and f∉V_n, yet g≡1∈V_n interpolates f at the sample points, so E[Y|XX]∈col(X).

failure_location.quote: Note that $\E[\bm Y| \XX]\in \col(\bm X)$ only if $f-f^*$ vanishes at $x_i$, i.e., $f\in V_n$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by the correct one: E[Y|XX]∈col(X) iff there exists g∈V_n with g(x_i)=f(x_i) for all i; or state f∈V_n only as a sufficient condition.
issues.overall_effect: The prose explanation of when the Christoffel least-squares estimator has no approximation bias is mathematically incorrect.
issues.title: False necessary condition for absence of least-squares bias
issues.why_classification: A local wording/correction in a non-formal explanation; no theorem or algorithmic guarantee depends on the false necessary condition.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for every $\delta\in [0, \frac{1}{m}]$ and $m\geq n$, $\mu$-a.s., \eqref{H-conv+} is a convex optimization problem with a finite optimal solution

issues.failure_explanation: For δ=0, feasible p may have zero entries, where Σ(p) is undefined and U(p) need not be invertible. Full column rank of W^{1/2}V only says that the rows collectively span V_n; a boundary allocation supported on a non-spanning subset makes U(p) singular.

failure_location.quote: Under the column-rank assumption on $\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm V$, $\bm U(\bm p)$ is invertible for $\bm p\in\mathcal P_m(\delta)$. Therefore, $H(\bm p)<\infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the lemma to δ∈(0,1/m], or define H by continuous extension and prove the δ=0 case separately.
issues.overall_effect: The δ=0 case of Lemma mkjh, including the stated sparse-optimal-solution claim at the boundary, is not established by the proof.
issues.title: Lemma mkjh proof assumes invertibility on the whole unregularized simplex
issues.why_classification: The defect is a boundary/degenerate hypothesis; the main reweighted results use δ>0, and a local restriction or limiting argument repairs the proof without changing the substantive guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: The linear dependence of the matrices R_iR_i^T gives a vector a with ∑a_iR_iR_i^T=0, but not necessarily ∑a_i=0. A perturbation of a probability vector must preserve ∑p_i=1; if ∑a_i≠0, q+ta is infeasible, and renormalization changes U(p) and the objective. The proof omits the required affine-dependence or minimal-support/scaling argument.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, there exists a direction $\bm a = (a_1, \ldots, a_m)^\top$ supported on $\text{supp}_{\delta}(\bm q^{*}_n)$ such that  $\sum_{i\in [m]}\frac{a_i}{\sigma^2(x_i)}R_iR^\top_i = 0$. Applying a perturbation argument for $\bm q^{*}_n$ along $\bm a$ yields another optimal solution that has a smaller $\delta$-support.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a minimal-support argument using the augmented vectors (1, R_iR_i^T/σ_i^2) and the homogeneity of the criterion, or correct the perturbation to a feasible direction; if the exact bound (n^2+n)/2 is not attainable, weaken it accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The support-size bound in Lemma mkjh is not established as written.
issues.title: Missing feasibility direction in support reduction for Lemma mkjh
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a nontrivial design-theoretic argument and may force a slight weakening of the stated support bound; it is not a one-line local fix, but it does not affect the global architecture of the paper.

issues.failure_explanation: Λ(·) is introduced as the spectrum of a matrix, but W^{1/2}V is m×n and rectangular, so its eigenvalue spectrum is not defined. The subsequent implication and condition-number bound only make sense if Λ denotes singular values.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define Λ to be the singular-value spectrum, or rewrite the event in terms of the singular values of W^{1/2}V.
issues.overall_effect: The conditioning event A in the main theorem is formally ill-defined as written.
issues.title: Event A in Theorem thm:main uses undefined spectrum of a rectangular matrix
issues.why_classification: The intended correction is forced by the later condition-number implication; all substantive estimates survive unchanged once the terminology is fixed.

issues.failure_explanation: J_n controls only the ratios of w(x)σ^2(x), while p_n^* also depends on √Φ_n(x). Thus min_i p_{n,i}^* can be much smaller than 1/(m√J_n). For instance, if wσ^2 is constant so J_n=1, but Φ_n(x_1)≫Φ_n(x_2), then p_{n,2}^*<1/m, so p_n^*∉P_m(1/m).

failure_location.quote: By setting $\delta \leq \frac{1}{m\sqrt{J_n}}$, it can be verified using \eqref{neyman} that $\bm p_n^*\in\mathcal P_m(\delta)$ so that $H(\bm q^{*}_n)\leq H(\bm p^*_n)\leq G(\bm p^*_n)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the uniform condition by δ≤min_i p_{n,i}^* or add assumptions bounding the ratios of Φ_n(x_i); weaken the remark accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed variance comparison H(q_n^*)≤G(p_n^*) under the stated small δ, and the associated interpretation that reweighted allocation dominates non-reweighted variance, is unsupported.
issues.title: False uniform δ-feasibility claim for Neyman allocation in Remark rem:compare
issues.why_classification: The correction withdraws a substantive promised regime for comparing the two allocations. The repair is contained but requires an additional feasibility condition or a nontrivial bound, so it is more than a local typo.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Choosing $l\geq \log(1/\delta)/\log 2$ and noting $2/\log 2<3$ yields the desired result.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof requires l disjoint blocks of size k, so lk≤n. With natural logarithms, n>1.5 log(1/δ)k does not imply floor(n/k)≥ceil(log(1/δ)/log2) for all δ. For example, δ=0.3 requires l=2, but n≈1.81k satisfies the stated hypothesis while allowing only one full block, giving success probability at most 1/2 rather than 1-δ.

failure_location.quote: if $k = \lceil2\e^{-2}\|\sigma\|^2_{L^2_\mu}\rceil$ and $n> 1.5\log(1/\delta)k$, where $\sigma^2(x) = \mathrm{Var}[g(x, Z)| x]$, then with probability at least $1-\delta$,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Increase the multiplicative constant from 1.5 to a sufficient value such as 3, or state the exact block-count condition n≥ceil(log(1/δ)/log2)k.
issues.overall_effect: The high-probability approximation bound in Theorem thm:rb is not valid under the stated sample-size condition for some δ.
issues.title: Insufficient sample-size constant in Theorem thm:rb boosting argument
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local constant-factor correction in the hypothesis; the logarithmic dependence and the conclusion survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To find a substitute of $\widetilde{f}_n$ in $V_n$, based on $\bm\theta$, we define $f_{n} = g_n-\sum_{i\in [s]}\theta_ih_{i}\in V_{n}$.
with $k = \lceil C_1 r(\log r)^3\rceil$ and for any $\delta>0$, if $n> 10\log (1/\delta) k$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts that some k-sparse combination in \bar V_{n,k} has error at most 24√{rτ_{r+1}}. The proof instead constructs f_n using s=n/2 differences h_i, hence up to all n random basis functions, and never shows that the resulting coefficients have support size ≤k. The sparsity parameter k appears only in a lower bound on n; no k-sparse block selection or sparsification is proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either construct a k-sparse element of \bar{V}_{n,k} (or adjust k to the actual support) with the claimed error and a valid high-probability argument, or weaken the conclusion to the full subspace V_n with the corresponding sample-size/probability change.
issues.overall_effect: The refined adaptive random-subspace approximation guarantee, and the abstract/introduction/numerical claims relying on it, are unsupported. The advertised k-sparse approximation capacity of V_n is not established.
issues.title: Theorem thm:984 does not establish the k-sparse approximation guarantee
issues.why_classification: The central quantitative guarantee changes from a k-sparse adaptive approximation to an unproved dense approximation; no comparable stated result survives without new proof architecture or major weakening.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Combining \eqref{yonghuo} and \eqref{yonghuo2} yields that, with probability at least $0.4$, $\lambda_{\min}(\bm L^\top\bm L)\geq s/2$.
Since $\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde{\bm\zeta}_i\widetilde{\bm\zeta}_i^\top) = \|\widetilde{\bm\zeta}_i\|_2^2\leq rT^2$, by the matrix Chernoff bound \cite{tropp2012user}

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed inequality bounds the probability of the good event λ_min≥0.5s by at most 0.5. The subsequent union-bound argument, however, treats \eqref{yonghuo2} as a bound on the bad event λ_min<0.5s. Matrix Chernoff gives a small upper bound for the lower-tail failure probability, not for the complementary good event.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the event in \eqref{yonghuo2} to λ_min≤0.5s, or equivalently bound 1-P(λ_min≥0.5s), and then use that bound in the union argument.
issues.overall_effect: The concentration step producing the constant-probability lower bound on λ_min(L^TL) is invalid as written.
issues.title: Matrix Chernoff inequality has the wrong direction in Theorem thm:984 proof
issues.why_classification: The defect is a local inequality-direction error with an obvious correction; it does not by itself require a new proof architecture.
